coverage_gaps: The merged universe is still strongest in defense subtier suppliers and grid/electrical infrastructure; tariff-specific beneficiaries, specialty contractors, inspection/testing firms, and compliance software remain under-mapped.
Most company-level exposure claims outside the provided Layer 1B defense candidates are hypotheses or inferences and require filing-level validation in Layer 2.
Rare-earth magnet compliance needs jurisdiction-level parsing: later work must separate mine origin, oxide/feedstock origin, alloying, magnet production, final assembly, and defense qualification.

Semiconductor quartz chokepoint exposure is hard to map to public equities because the most direct assets are private or subsidiaries; public exposure may be indirect through wafer, crucible, specialty-chemical, or equipment supply chains.
Current market caps, liquidity, analyst coverage, valuation, and public-listing status were not live-validated in this merge step.
Election and policy scenarios are not yet modeled; later layers should split by appropriations, agency rules, tariffs, waivers, domestic-content definitions, and committee control.
The universe intentionally includes reference leaders, but they should not crowd out the underfollowed lane in later evidence validation.

memory_update.text: Politics theme should remain framed as policy mechanisms: appropriations, tariffs, domestic-content rules, export controls, infrastructure bills, sourcing compliance, and regulated capacity rather than party headlines.
Lower-tier defense suppliers are the highest-priority underfollowed lane because public evidence says DoD supply chains extend five to six tiers and visibility weakens beyond tier two.
Rare-earth magnet compliance should be researched by feedstock origin and qualification status, not just mine ownership or factory location.
Grid and utility-qualified components remain a strong second-order lane where public capex, long manufacturing cycles, and switching costs can create chokepoints.
Supply-chain visibility and trade-compliance software may become investable second-order beneficiaries if tariffs, sanctions, and sourcing-resilience rules keep fragmenting.
Layer 2 must live-validate all market caps, listing status, liquidity, current filings, backlog, customer concentration, policy exposure, and valuation before any candidate can be promoted.

Semiconductor high-purity quartz has strong chokepoint logic but weak direct public-equity mapping; later work should verify whether indirect wafer, crucible, specialty-chemical, or graphite suppliers have meaningful exposure.

summary: Layer 1C merges the Politics theme into a diversified initial research universe organized around policy-driven chokepoints rather than party headlines. The strongest nodes are lower-tier defense industrial-base suppliers, rare-earth magnet and compliant feedstock transition assets, grid and utility-qualified electrification suppliers, trade/supply-chain compliance tools, and obscure semiconductor materials dependencies. The universe intentionally balances reference leaders with underfollowed small/mid-cap or niche second-order candidates. Scores reflect Serenity relevance for next-stage research, not investment recommendations.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
